cg-api-service::no-privileged-containers.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains code execution within the privileged container could directly access the host kernel and bypass all container isolation mechanisms, allowing them to escape the container, compromise other containers, access sensitive host resources, and potentially exfiltrate payment card data or install persistent backdoors. This elevated capability eliminates the security boundary between the application and the underlying infrastructure.
cg-api-service::no-privileged-containers.business_risk: Running containers in privileged mode violates PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requirements for least privilege access, creating a critical compliance violation that could result in failed audits, significant fines, and loss of payment processing authorization. A container escape could lead to direct access to cardholder data and complete infrastructure compromise.
remediation_steps: Remove the 'privileged: true' flag from the cg-api-service container deployment configuration
Replace privileged mode with specific Linux capabilities required by the application using '--cap-add' for only necessary capabilities (e.g., NET_BIND_SERVICE) instead of granting all capabilities
Test the application with restricted capabilities and apply security context constraints including runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and appropriate seccomp/AppArmor profiles
Redeploy the container and verify functionality, then update container orchestration policies to enforce non-privileged mode across all workloads
cg-api-service::no-privileged-containers.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requires implementation of the principle of least privilege by restricting access to system resources and data by processes to the minimum required, which prohibits running containers with all host kernel capabilities enabled through privileged mode.

cg-data-processor::no-new-privileges.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains initial access to the container through a vulnerability in the application or a compromised dependency could exploit the absence of the no-new-privileges flag to escalate privileges using setuid/setgid binaries or kernel exploits. This would allow them to break out of the container's security context and potentially compromise the host system or access sensitive data processed by the container.
cg-data-processor::no-new-privileges.business_risk: Without the no-new-privileges restriction, a compromised container can escalate to higher privilege levels, enabling unauthorized access to sensitive payment card data and system resources in violation of PCI-DSS segmentation and access control requirements. This increases the risk of data breaches and regulatory non-compliance penalties.
remediation_steps: Update the container security context in the deployment manifest (Dockerfile, Kubernetes pod spec, or container runtime configuration) to include securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
Alternatively, add the --security-opt=no-new-privileges flag to the docker run command or equivalent container orchestration configuration
Rebuild and redeploy the cg-data-processor container with the updated security configuration, then verify the setting is applied using container inspection tools
cg-data-processor::no-new-privileges.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requires that system configuration standards must include disabling unnecessary services and functions; the no-new-privileges setting is a mandatory OS-level security hardening control to prevent privilege escalation.

cg-data-processor::read-only-root-filesy.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains container access could modify system binaries, inject malicious code, or establish persistence by writing to the root filesystem. This allows them to execute unauthorized commands, escalate privileges, or maintain backdoor access even after container restart.
cg-data-processor::read-only-root-filesy.business_risk: A writable root filesystem increases the blast radius of container compromises and violates PCI-DSS requirements for secure configuration management, potentially leading to compliance failures and data breach exposure affecting cardholder data.
remediation_steps: Add 'securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true' to the cg-data-processor container specification in the deployment manifest
Create emptyDir volumes for any application paths requiring write access (e.g., /tmp, /var/tmp, application cache directories)
Mount these emptyDir volumes to the container at the necessary paths and update application configuration to use these writable locations
Test the container to ensure all functionality works correctly with a read-only root filesystem before deploying to production
cg-data-processor::read-only-root-filesy.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requires that all system components be configured securely with only necessary services, ports, and protocols enabled; a writable root filesystem increases unnecessary write permissions that violate secure configuration principles.

cg-data-processor::drop-all-capabilities.attack_scenario: An attacker exploiting a vulnerability in the cg-data-processor application could leverage the unrestricted Linux capabilities to perform privilege escalation attacks, such as modifying kernel parameters, accessing raw network sockets, or mounting filesystems. With all capabilities intact, the attacker could break out of container isolation and compromise the host system or adjacent containers.
cg-data-processor::drop-all-capabilities.business_risk: This configuration violates PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requirement to implement least privilege access controls, creating a compliance violation that could result in failed audits, fines, and loss of payment card processing authorization. An exploited container with full capabilities could lead to unauthorized access to cardholder data and other sensitive systems.
remediation_steps: Update the container security policy or pod specification to add 'securityContext.capabilities.drop: [ALL]' to drop all Linux capabilities
Verify the application functionality after dropping all capabilities and add back only explicitly required capabilities using 'securityContext.capabilities.add' if needed
Rebuild and redeploy the container image with the updated security configuration to the cg-data-processor deployment
cg-data-processor::drop-all-capabilities.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requires that access control mechanisms restrict users to only the minimum required privileges to perform their job functions; dropping all Linux capabilities enforces the principle of least privilege at the container level.

cg-legacy-service::no-new-privileges.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains code execution within the container (via vulnerability exploitation or supply chain compromise) could escalate privileges by leveraging setuid binaries or kernel exploits, since the no-new-privileges flag is not enforced. This allows privilege escalation from a lower-privileged container process to potentially root access, enabling lateral movement to the host system or other containers.
cg-legacy-service::no-new-privileges.business_risk: Without the no-new-privileges restriction, a compromised container can escalate to root privileges and breach the isolation boundary, leading to unauthorized access to sensitive payment card data and violating PCI-DSS security controls. This creates compliance violations, potential data breach liability, and failure of required security assessments.
remediation_steps: Add the securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false field to the cg-legacy-service container specification in the Pod/Deployment manifest
Alternatively, set the no-new-privileges flag in the container runtime security options or add --security-opt=no-new-privileges:true to Docker/containerd configurations
Deploy the updated configuration and verify the setting is active by inspecting the running container's security context using 'docker inspect' or 'kubectl describe pod'
cg-legacy-service::no-new-privileges.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requires that all system components must be hardened and configured with security settings that restrict unnecessary access and functionality, including disabling privilege escalation in containerized environments.

cg-legacy-service::read-only-root-filesy.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains code execution within the cg-legacy-service container can modify system binaries, inject malware, or install persistence mechanisms on the writable root filesystem. These modifications would survive container restarts and could be used to establish long-term access or pivot to other systems on the network.
cg-legacy-service::read-only-root-filesy.business_risk: A compromised container with write access to the root filesystem creates a compliance violation of PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requirements for secure configuration standards. This exposes the organization to potential data breaches, regulatory fines, and audit failures during PCI-DSS assessments.
remediation_steps: Add securityContext.readOnlyRootFilesystem: true to the cg-legacy-service container specification in the deployment manifest
Identify and create emptyDir volumes for any runtime-required writable paths (e.g., /tmp, /var/log, /var/cache) and mount them as temporary filesystems
Test the application thoroughly in a staging environment to ensure all required write operations are directed to mounted volumes, then deploy to production
cg-legacy-service::read-only-root-filesy.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requires that configuration standards define security settings for system components, including enforcing read-only root filesystems to reduce the attack surface and prevent unauthorized modification of system files.

cg-legacy-service::drop-all-capabilities.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains code execution inside the container can exploit retained Linux capabilities (such as CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_NET_ADMIN, or CAP_SYS_PTRACE) to escalate privileges, escape the container isolation, or modify host kernel parameters. This allows lateral movement to the host system or other containers sharing the same kernel.
cg-legacy-service::drop-all-capabilities.business_risk: Failure to drop all capabilities violates PCI-DSS requirement for least privilege access controls, increasing the blast radius of any container compromise and enabling potential cardholder data exfiltration or system-wide breach. This creates a critical compliance gap that could result in audit failures and regulatory penalties.
remediation_steps: Update the container security context in the deployment manifest to add 'securityContext.capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]'
Verify the cg-legacy-service Dockerfile or pod specification explicitly drops all capabilities and only adds back specific required capabilities if necessary
Test the container with the applied security context to ensure all required functionality remains operational
cg-legacy-service::drop-all-capabilities.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requires that access control mechanisms restrict user and process access to system resources based on the principle of least privilege, which includes dropping unnecessary Linux capabilities from containerized processes.

cg-api-service::no-privileged-containers.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains code execution within the privileged container can access the host kernel and escape the container boundary to compromise the entire host system and other containers. With privileged mode enabled, the attacker can mount the host filesystem, modify kernel parameters, and pivot to adjacent systems on the network without requiring additional privilege escalation techniques.
cg-api-service::no-privileged-containers.business_risk: Running containers in privileged mode violates PCI-DSS requirement 7.2.1 by granting excessive system privileges that enable container escape and lateral movement, potentially exposing cardholder data environments to unauthorized access. This misconfiguration creates a critical compliance violation that could result in failed PCI-DSS audits, substantial fines, and mandatory re-certification requirements.
remediation_steps: Remove the 'privileged: true' flag from the cg-api-service container deployment manifest or docker-compose configuration
If specific capabilities are required, replace privileged mode with granular Linux capability assignments using the 'capabilities' field (e.g., only add CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE if needed)
Redeploy the container with the updated configuration and verify functionality without privileged mode access
cg-api-service::no-privileged-containers.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requires that access to system components must be restricted based on the principle of least privilege; running containers in privileged mode violates this by granting unnecessary elevated permissions beyond what the application requires.

cg-data-processor::no-new-privileges.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains code execution within the container through a vulnerable application could exploit this misconfiguration to escalate privileges by leveraging setuid binaries or kernel vulnerabilities that would normally be blocked by the no-new-privileges flag. This allows the attacker to break out of container isolation and potentially compromise the host system or other containers.

Verify the remediation by confirming the container is running with no-new-privileges flag enabled
cg-data-processor::no-new-privileges.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requires all system components to have security configurations that restrict functionality to necessary services only, and the no-new-privileges flag is a required control to prevent privilege escalation within containerized environments.

Test the application thoroughly to ensure it functions correctly with a read-only root filesystem
Deploy the updated container image to your registry and redeploy affected container instances
cg-data-processor::read-only-root-filesy.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requires that all system components are configured securely according to vendor recommendations; read-only root filesystems are a fundamental hardening control to prevent unauthorized modification of system files and binaries.

This allows lateral movement to the host system or other containers, potentially compromising cardholder data stored or processed by the application.

cg-data-processor::drop-all-capabilities.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requires that users and processes are limited to the minimum set of required privileges, which includes dropping all unnecessary Linux capabilities from containers to prevent privilege escalation.

cg-legacy-service::no-new-privileges.attack_scenario: An attacker who gains initial access to the container through a vulnerability in the application can exploit setuid/setgid binaries or capability escalation to elevate privileges to root or other users. cg-legacy-service::no-new-privileges.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requires that all system components must be configured to prevent unnecessary and insecure services, protocols, and daemons; the no-new-privileges setting prevents privilege escalation through setuid/setgid binaries, enforcing secure default container behavior.

cg-legacy-service::read-only-root-filesy.business_risk: A compromised container with writable root filesystem violates PCI-DSS requirements for system hardening and creates audit findings that could impact compliance certification. cg-legacy-service::read-only-root-filesy.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-2.2.1 requires that configuration standards address the security of systems and services, including implementing read-only root filesystems to prevent unauthorized modification of system files and enforce the principle of least privilege.

Apply the updated manifest and restart the cg-legacy-service pods to enforce the capability restrictions
cg-legacy-service::drop-all-capabilities.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requires that system components be configured to run with the minimum set of privileges necessary, and containers must drop all Linux capabilities by default to enforce least privilege access.

cg-api-service::no-privileged-containers.pci_requirement_detail: PCI-DSS-v4.0-7.2.1 requires that access to system components is restricted based on need-to-know principle; running containers in privileged mode grants unnecessary elevated access that violates least privilege access controls.
